metadata.note: The Southbridge and Sturbridge Street Railway: a village-to-village electric street railway in south-central Worcester County, MA, linking Fiskdale (Sturbridge) to Sandersdale (Southbridge) via Sturbridge Center, Globe Village and Southbridge Center, 1896-circa 1930. Organized as an independent company, it was built with an eye toward forming part of a through Worcester-Hartford route (the two cities had no direct steam railroad connection), a plan that never fully materialized, though the line itself ran successfully for over three decades under three owners: the original independent company, the Worcester and Southbridge Street Railway (which absorbed it in 1901-1905), and finally the Worcester Consolidated Street Railway (from the 1911 four-company merger) until abandonment sometime in the mid-to-late 1920s.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester_Consolidated_Street_Railway -- Southbridge and Sturbridge organization/opening date and mileage, ownership chain (Worcester and Southbridge control from 1901/1902, New Haven purchase May 1904, merger Jan 1905), Worcester Consolidated's 1911 four-company merger and general 1924-1930 rural abandonment wave

https://bigalumlake.org/chapter-9/ -- route description (Fiskdale - Sturbridge Center - Globe Village - Southbridge Center - Fairview Park Road/Route 131), 1906 Fiskdale substation, 1901 timetable fare/running-time detail, local color on the line's effect on Big Alum Lake's development
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandersdale,_Massachusetts -- Sandersdale's location on Southbridge's east side along Route 131/East Main Street past the AO Rotary
OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overpass (overpass.openstreetmap.fr) -- all route geometry, present-day street centrelines
Nominatim (OpenStreetMap) -- geocoding of Fiskdale, Sturbridge Center, Globe Village, Southbridge Center and Sandersdale
metadata.geometry_sources: Street-centreline routing throughout -- see each feature's geometry_source/geometry_quality. No railway-tagged remnant of this line survives in OSM.
not_yet_sourced: The specific year this branch's passenger service was abandoned is not sourced; 1930 is used as a placeholder within the documented 1924-1930 general abandonment window for Worcester Consolidated's rural lines.
Headway_min (60) is an unsourced estimate for all three eras; only the ~18 km/h speed estimate has a real (1901 timetable) source, and only for the Southbridge-Sturbridge leg specifically.

The exact street-by-street routing through Sturbridge Center and Southbridge Center, and whether the line used the original alignment or the later Route 131 realignment near Sandersdale, are not verified against period maps.

metadata.horsecar_audit: N/A -- opened 1896 as an electric line from the start; no horsecar predecessor found in sources.

properties.line: Southbridge and Sturbridge: Fiskdale - Sturbridge Center - Globe Village - Southbridge - Sandersdale
properties.speed_source: A dated (1901) company timetable detail survives for the Southbridge-Sturbridge leg specifically: fare 5 cents, running time 15 minutes -- roughly 18 km/h over that ~4.5 mile stretch. Applied here as a single average for the whole Fiskdale-Sandersdale line; no source gives a separate speed for the Globe Village-Sandersdale extension.

segments.note: Organized Feb 18, 1896; opened Aug 29, 1896 as a 7.44-mile line between Fiskdale (a village of Sturbridge) and Sandersdale (a village of Southbridge), running southeast from Fiskdale through Sturbridge Center, Globe Village and Southbridge Center. Intended as part of a through route between Worcester and Hartford, CT, which had no direct steam railroad connection. A 1901 timetable shows the Southbridge-Sturbridge fare as 5 cents for a 15-minute run. Headway is an unsourced estimate.

properties.geometry_source: Routed along present-day street centrelines from OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overpass (overpass.openstreetmap.fr): shortest path along the road network from Fiskdale (Sturbridge) through Sturbridge Center and Globe Village to Southbridge Center, mostly on Main Street with brief stretches signed 'Old Southbridge Road'/'Old Sturbridge Road' -- plausibly closer to the original alignment than the modern Route 131 realignment, given the names -- then continuing via Main Street, the Southbridge Rotary and East Main Street to Sandersdale. No abandoned railway/streetcar trace survives in OSM for this line (it was a true street railway, running in the roadway throughout), so this is street-centreline routing rather than a track alignment. Passes within 175m of Globe Village and 200m of Sturbridge Center as geocoded. 702 points, 10.82 km (6.72 mi) one-way against the 7.44 mi Fiskdale-Sandersdale figure the company itself reported at opening -- a reasonable match; the shortfall is most likely the terminal/yard trackage at each end plus minor local deviations this routing can't recover. Checked for self-intersection using cumulative along-path distance (not just point proximity, which false-positives heavily on a dense, nearly-straight road) -- none found.
properties.geometry_quality: STREET-CENTRELINE ROUTING, not a traced track alignment -- there is nothing else to trace against, since no railway-tagged remnant of this line survives in OpenStreetMap. Which side of the street the single track ran, the exact routing through Sturbridge Center and Southbridge Center (both dense village cores where several streets converge), and the original vs. Route-131-era alignment near Sandersdale are not verified against period maps or Sanborn atlases. No leg is a straight-line placeholder.

properties.line: Worcester and Southbridge: Fiskdale - Sturbridge Center - Globe Village - Southbridge - Sandersdale
properties.speed_source: A dated (1901) company timetable detail survives for the Southbridge-Sturbridge leg specifically: fare 5 cents, running time 15 minutes -- roughly 18 km/h over that ~4.5 mile stretch. Applied here as a single average for the whole Fiskdale-Sandersdale line; no source gives a separate speed for the Globe Village-Sandersdale extension.

segments.note: The Worcester and Southbridge Street Railway obtained control of the Southbridge and Sturbridge in 1901 and began operating it in January 1902 -- the split used here, matching this dataset's convention of coloring by whoever actually ran the trains, not the later formal paperwork. The New York, New Haven and Hartford Railroad purchased the Worcester and Southbridge (along with the Worcester, Rochdale and Charlton Depot, and the Southbridge and Sturbridge itself) in May 1904, and the two smaller companies were formally merged into the Worcester and Southbridge on Jan 9, 1905, ending the Southbridge and Sturbridge's separate corporate existence. Headway is an unsourced estimate.

properties.line: Worcester Consolidated: Fiskdale - Sturbridge Center - Globe Village - Southbridge - Sandersdale
properties.speed_source: A dated (1901) company timetable detail survives for the Southbridge-Sturbridge leg specifically: fare 5 cents, running time 15 minutes -- roughly 18 km/h over that ~4.5 mile stretch. Applied here as a single average for the whole Fiskdale-Sandersdale line; no source gives a separate speed for the Globe Village-Sandersdale extension.

segments.note: The Worcester and Southbridge was one of four companies merged into the Worcester Consolidated Street Railway on May 3, 1911. No source found gives a specific abandonment date for this branch -- Worcester Consolidated's rural/suburban lines were abandoned in a wave between 1924 and 1930 as the company retrenched to its most profitable routes (Southbridge itself is named as one of the surviving destinations in the mid-1920s cutback, but that doesn't confirm this Sturbridge branch specifically survived to the end of the window), so 1930 is used here as a placeholder end date, flagged in this file's not_yet_sourced. Headway is an unsourced estimate.
